newsitem.title: UK: Princess Diana's ex-maid accepts cash settlement.
newsitem.headline: Princess Diana's ex-maid accepts cash settlement.

text.p: A former maid of Diana, Princess of Wales, who claimed unfair dismissal, received undisclosed compensation on Wednesday as the case was settled out of court.
Sylvia McDermott, 46, had filed the case after she was dismissed without warning from the princess's household last September.

There had been speculation that Diana might be called to give evidence in the case, but the world's most photographed woman did not appear for the cameramen gathered outside the south London industrial tribunal.
Lawyers reached an out-of-court settlement after last-minute negotiations.
Diana's lawyer, David Pannick, said in a statement to the tribunal: "We are happy to tell the tribunal that the parties have reached agreement."
He said McDermott, who earned 9,000 pounds ($14,550) a year while she worked for the princess, had accepted "a sum of compensation".
"The parties have agreed that the sum shall remain confidential," he said.
McDermott said she was pleased with the agreement. She joined the household of the Prince and Princess of Wales in 1987 and stayed with the princess after the royal couple separated in 1992.
She is one of 28 staff who have left the service of the princess in recent years.
